 Coram:Honourable Mrs. Justice M. K. Thakker
 Date : 24/03/2026
 Judgment

1. The present application is filed seeking quashment of the FIR No.11192011200767 of 2020 registered with Bopal Police Station, Ahmedabad Rural for the offences under Sections 420, 384,
389 and 506(2) of the Indian Penal Code, stating the date of occurrence as 01.06.2019 and the registration of the FIR as 28.08.2020.

sentences.text: As per the impugned FIR, it is alleged that in the year 2016, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/77/2021 JUDGMENT DATED: 24/03/2026 undefined when the complainant had gone to Delhi for preparation of UPSC exam in the month of June-July 2019, the applicant had contacted the complainant through Telegram / Social Media and shown her desire to pursue the UPSC exam.
On a request being made by the applicant, the complainant made arrangements for her stay at Delhi and the applicant came to Delhi along with her mother.
During that period, the complainant and the accused used to talk with each other and they fell in love with each other, as well as developed physical relations.
As per the FIR, the complainant had lent some money to the applicant and subsequently, threats were issued to falsely implicate him in a case of rape.
The said FIR is the subject matter of challenge before this Court.

3. Heard the learned advocate Mr. Fouzan Soniwala for the applicant, the learned advocate Mr.
Dharm Raval for the complainant and the learned APP Mr. Ronak Rawal for the State.
4.

Learned advocate Mr. Soniwala submits that to make it appear that the applicant has extorted money from the complainant, the amounts were transferred without having the knowledge of the applicant through Google Pay.

It is submitted NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/77/2021 JUDGMENT DATED: 24/03/2026 undefined that immediately on realizing the transfer being made by the complainant, the applicant had sent back the said amount through Google Pay.

It is further submitted that a complaint has been filed by the present applicant against the complainant herein for the offence under Section 376 of the IPC and to take revenge for the said complaint, a false FIR was filed before the Bopal Police Station, Ahmedabad alleging the accusations of Sections 384, 389,
506(2) and 420 of the IPC.
It is submitted that the FIR was delayed by more than one year and without any explanation offered in the FIR.
Continuation of the process would be nothing but an abuse of the process of law and in that background, it is prayed to allow the present application by quashing and setting aside the impugned FIR.

5. Per contra, the learned advocate Mr. Raval for the original complainant has submitted that the present applicant is habitual in making false allegations of rape and she has filed FIRs of a similar nature against four other accused.

It is further submitted that against the complainant, the FIR which was lodged was resulted into an acquittal, as well as the learned Trial Court has ordered to prosecute the present applicant for forgery.

It is NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/77/2021 JUDGMENT DATED: 24/03/2026 undefined submitted that there is one more FIR which was registered against 4 accused, which was culminated into the Criminal Case No.67 of 2019, where also all accused were acquitted of the charges punishable under Sections 354, 354-A read with Section 34 of the IPC.

It is submitted that thereafter, a Police Officer was implicated as a accused in a criminal case which was filed before the learned Civil Court, at Murtizapur which was also dismissed due to the absence of the complainant.
It is submitted that due to the protection granted by this Court, the FIR was not investigated and a charge-sheet is yet not filed.

Therefore, at this stage, no interference may be called for and the present application deserves to be rejected.
6.

The learned APP Mr. Rawal for the State, in support of submissions made by the learned advocate Mr. Raval for the complainant, has placed on record the screenshots of the mobile of the applicant,
wherein messages in abusive language which were sent to the complainant have been found.

2 further submitted that, apart from the transactions which were returned back, there is evidence on record that the present applicant had extort money to the extent of Rs.53,000/- from the applicant.

sentences.text:
It is NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/77/2021 JUDGMENT DATED: 24/03/2026 undefined further submitted that as the applicant is in the habit of filing false cases against various persons,
the investigation is required to be concluded and the same is required to be put an end to logical end.
7. Having considered the submissions made by the learned advocates for the respective parties as well as the material placed on record by the State and the complainant, it emerges that the present applicant has lodged an FIR under Section 376 of the IPC on 19.11.2020 and during the trial, the complainant was acquitted and the learned Court has made following observations;
"18.
Though it is also settled law that the testimony of prosecutrix if found to be trustworthy and predible, does not require any independent corroboration.
However the testimony of prosecutrix herein is not of sterling quality for the reasons as already discussed as above.

Rather, it is evident from record that prosecutrix made a false statement before this court as it has got proved that the hotel CPS Castle, where the second incident of alleged rape took place, was shut down from 22.03.2020 due to ovid and same got re-opened only on 16.08.2020.

To quote Hon'ble Karnataka High Court ("Nirmala v. Rakminibar, AIR 1994 Kar 247") "there are two types of liar in the world - - one artful liar and another clumsy NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/77/2021 JUDGMENT DATED: 24/03/2026 undefined liar."
Prosecutrix herein shall fall under the latter class, because though she told the lie, she told it clumsily which on the face of it stands proved to be not believable.
19. Accordingly, accused persons namely Ritesh Chaudhary, Virender @Viren, Sunita and Reena stand acquitted in the instant case of all the charges levelled against them.

They are directed to furnish bail bond in terms of section 437A Cr.PC.
20.
Before parting, I may hasten to add here that the career of a bright young student (Ritesh) appears to have been lost in the heap of false accusations.
It takes one's lifetime to build a reputation but only few lies to destroy the same.

Therefore in my view, an acquittal simplicitor can not recompense the agony of accused Ritesh who had to undergo the trauma of a trial for such a henious offence based on a false story of sexual assault.

Considering the fact that it has got proved on record that prosecutrix has made false statement before this court, let a complaint under section 340 CrPC for offence of perjury be sent against her to the court of Ld. CMM (Central)
by the Reader of this court."

7.1 It also emerges from the record that the present applicant has also lodged an FIR on 22.11.2018 against four different persons alleging the accusations under Section 354 and 354-A read with Section 34 of the IPC.
The learned Trial Court has made following observations while rendering the judgment of the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/77/2021 JUDGMENT DATED: 24/03/2026 undefined acquittal.

sentences.text: "Looking into the evidence of PW-3 and PW-4, to whom the prosecution has brought as an eye witnesses, there came forth that, neither any incident of use of criminal force or assault by the accused to the informant, nor any incident of physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures by the accused to the informant has taken place.
The best evidence could have been the informant herself but despite of efforts taken by the prosecution, informant is not examine due to her absence from her address given.

So far as the evidence of PW-5 is concerned,
he is only the filing officer and in absence of informant, it cannot be said that, FIR is duly proved.

PW-7 10 has also admitted that informant was caught while cheating and was rusticated for the same and thus, considering the evidence of PW-3 and 4,
the strong probability of lodging false FIR against the accused pops- up.
Except PW-5 and PW-6, none has supported the prosecution.

But, it is the cardinal principle of criminal law that, prosecution has to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt, wherein in case in hand it fails in and thus, considering the reasons discussed above, it cannot be said that, accused have committed any of the alleged offences and thus, finding to all these points is recorded accordingly in negative."
7.2

The applicant herein is also one of the complainants in the Criminal Case No.857 of 2020 filed before the learned Civil Court NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/77/2021 JUDGMENT DATED:
24/03/2026 undefined at Murtizapur for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)
(i)(n), 377, 417 and 506 of the IPC; there also the learned Trial Court has acquitted the accused vide judgment dated 06.05.2023.

sentences.text: 7.3 The bank details which are placed on record also suggest that there are money transactions between the present applicant and the complainant.

It is submitted by the learned advocate for the applicant that the said transactions were made without having the knowledge of the present applicant; however, the same being a disputed question of fact, is required to be investigated and tried by the learned trial court.

7.4 Considering the circumstances discussed hereinabove, it emerges that the present applicant is habitual in making false allegations of serious offences against persons who are subsequently acquitted, destroying the life of young persons by making the false allegation of rape.
Registration of an FIR cannot be said to be an abuse of the process of law.
In that background, this Court has also referred to the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, reported in 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335.

sentences.text: The case of the applicant NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/77/2021 JUDGMENT DATED: 24/03/2026 undefined does not fall into any criteria of the above case.
In that background, the present application deserves to be dismissed.
8. Resultantly, the present application is dismissed.
Notice is discharged.
